patients.label: 20-year-old primigravida at 39 weeks 6 days with term abdominal ectopic pregnancy initially misdiagnosed as placenta previa

identity_evidence.quote: A 20-year-old primigravida at 39 weeks and 6 days of gestation

attribution_limitations: Gestational age is stated as 39 weeks and 6 days (also 39+6 weeks in the abstract) while ultrasonography at presentation gave an estimated gestational age of 36+6 weeks; the source does not reconcile the two. The 39 weeks and 6 days figure is the gestation at presentation and 36+6 weeks is an ultrasonographic estimate, so they are different measurements rather than one conflicting value.

The abstract says the emergency cesarean section was planned for suspected placenta previa, while the case report says it was planned due to the transverse lie in labor; the abdominal examination recorded no uterine contractions, and the source does not say when labor began. The two indications can coexist and are not treated as a conflict.

The neonatal cause of death is worded as respiratory failure, respiratory distress and respiratory distress with hypoxia in different sections; these are recorded as separate wordings without choosing one.
The other laboratory parameters called within normal limits are not named, although the preceding sentence lists the tests sent; the sent tests have no individual results.
Figure 1 is called in the sentence about placental histopathology while its caption describes an intraoperative photograph of an intact amniotic membrane attached to the omentum.

The abstract says cesarean section was converted to laparotomy, but the case text says only that the procedure was initiated under spinal anesthesia and converted to general anesthesia; it does not state that the cesarean section was completed.

claims.text: A 20-year-old primigravida at 39 weeks and 6 days of gestation, with regular antenatal visits at a provincial hospital, presented to a tertiary care center for delivery. Five antenatal check-ups had consistently diagnosed placenta previa and transverse lie, and she had no abdominal pain or vaginal bleeding. At presentation she was in fair condition with stable vital signs and normal cardiopulmonary findings, and a fetal heart rate of 136 bpm.

claims.text: An emergency cesarean section was planned due to the transverse lie in labor; she was counseled, consent was obtained and prophylactic antibiotics were given, and it was initiated under spinal anesthesia via a Pfannenstiel incision. An intact amniotic sac was found in the abdominal cavity with the placenta adhered to the greater omentum, left ovary and left fallopian tube; it was converted to general anesthesia and laparotomy. A live female neonate was delivered by breech extraction, and the placenta was separated and sent for histopathology.
